- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next period.
- After a sharp price spike (forecast > 85), model often overshoots and fails to correct; cap forecast at +5% above peak or adjust downward by 2–4% in next 3–5 days.
- If sentiment turns negative (≤0.33) mid-horizon, model often underreacts; increase forecast by 1–2% to counteract mean reversion bias.
- Model underestimates prices when sentiment is mixed (0.33–0.67) and recent history shows downward momentum; add 0.5–1.5% to forecast to align with mean reversion.
- For 30-day horizon, model consistently overpredicts early in the forecast window (days 1–7); apply a 1–2% downward bias to first 5 days.
- When sentiment history shows repeated negative sentiment (e.g., 3+ consecutive negative values), model tends to lag; add 0.5–1.5% to forecast to catch downward trend.
